runs: Choose which runs and references appear in every chart. References only apply to the nowcast charts.
lossscale: Raw shows the loss as logged. Relative divides each run's loss by its own starting loss (start) or by base Chronos-2 on the same blocks (base). Live run zooms the x range to the current run.
train: Quantile (pinball) loss on the training batches, as a rolling mean of 20 logged points. Lower is better. Faint dots are single logged values.
held: The same loss on held-out simulated blocks the model never trains on. Lower is better. The relative views use each saved checkpoint's loss on the full held-out set.
bysrc: Held-out loss split by data layout, at each held-out evaluation from step 0 (zero-shot). Colour is the layout and line style is the run.
biasline: The mean of each relation's 144 values (12 layers x 12 heads) at each step. Hover a line to see its min to max range across heads.
biasheat: One square per layer (row) x head (column). Red means that head attends more than base Chronos-2 to that kind of pair, blue less. A bias of 1 weights those pairs x2.7.
relations: self = a row with itself. same = a place's counts, lags and totals. up = a place to its country. down = a country to its places.
lr: Learning rate of each optimiser group against step. Rates fall linearly to zero at the final step. The dot marks the current step.
perf: WIS or CRPS relative to randomwalknowcast. Below 1 is better. One line per run across checkpoints, with the zero-shot and randomwalknowcast references.
nowcast: Median and 50% and 95% bands of each ticked run for the chosen nowcast date, against the truth. Line style runs from dotted (earliest checkpoint) to solid (latest).
wis: Mean score over the nowcast dates the ticked runs have in common: weighted interval score for quantile forecasts, sample CRPS for sample forecasts. Lower is better. Each WIS bar is split into dispersion (interval width), overprediction (truth below the intervals) and underprediction (truth above), shades of the row's colour as in the paper; hover a part for its value.
logwis: The same WIS on the log scale: of log(x + 1) of the truth and of each quantile, as the shared scorer takes log WIS. It weighs relative errors, so small and large counts count alike. Split into the same three parts.
coverage: Share of truths inside the 50% and 95% intervals. The dashed lines mark the nominal 0.5 and 0.95.
biasscore: Mean of 1 minus 2 times the forecast CDF at the truth, from -1 (forecast too low) to +1 (too high). 0 is unbiased.
t_step: The trainer's current optimiser step, and how many simulations that is.
t_rate: Training speed over the last 30 minutes.
t_next: Simulations trained so far of the next checkpoint's size, and when it is due. A checkpoint already written and still being scored at its size is named below with the time it was written.
t_eta: Time to the final checkpoint at the recent training speed.
t_lr: Current learning rate of each optimiser group.
t_trainer: Whether the trainer process is running.
t_log: Time of the last training log line. It turns red after 10 minutes.
learnlevel: Held-out loss on all held-out simulated blocks at each checkpoint, by level (leaf, intermediate, national), divided by that level's loss at step 0. Each level is scored with the other rows of its blocks masked. Below 1 means fine-tuning helps that level; good is every line falling and none rising above 1.
learnlayer: How far the LoRA adapter has moved each encoder layer from base Chronos-2: the Frobenius norm of the scaled update B·A, a layer's time and group attention modules added in quadrature. One line per checkpoint. It shows where the model changes, not whether it improves: expect steady growth that slows as the learning rate falls, with no one layer running away.
learnkind: The same update size split by kind of module: time attention (along each series), group attention (across the series of a block) and the output layer, at each checkpoint. Growing group attention means the model is learning how places relate; growth that levels off late in the run is expected as the learning rate falls to zero.
wisbars: Mean weighted interval score (WIS) of each checkpoint and reference on the forecasts they all made, split into its three parts, which sum to it: dispersion (the width of the intervals), underprediction (truth above them) and overprediction (truth below them). Lower is better. Good is the checkpoints' bars shrinking with size and ending below the references, without trading spread for one-sided misses.
